papers.title: Hybrid intelligent modeling for calibrated business and financial risk classification: a decision-support perspective
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a calibration-aware hybrid framework for large-scale business and financial risk classification, addressing heterogeneous features, nonlinear relationships, temporal distribution shifts, class imbalance and unreliable probability estimates. Design/methodology/approach The hybrid multi-agent quantum neural transformer (H–MAQNT) combines a tabular transformer, domain-specialized variational quantum neural network (VQNN) agents and adaptive attention-based fusion. It uses leakage-controlled preprocessing, domain-informed features, imbalance-aware training, validation-only model selection and calibration and quantum-aware multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization (QMFBO) for cost-aware tuning. Findings On temporally held-out LendingClub and IEEE–CIS future test periods, H–MAQNT outperforms strong gradient-boosted, neural and transformer-based baselines in discrimination and probability quality. It improves the receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC–AUC) by approximately 1.1–1.3 percentage points over the strongest Transformer-based baselines, lowers expected calibration error (ECE) on both data sets and reduces high-fidelity optimization evaluations by 35% relative to single-fidelity Bayesian optimization. Research limitations/implications The evidence is based on two public data sets and classically simulated quantum circuits. Future work should test additional institutions, rolling time windows, physical hardware and prospective drift and recalibration policies. Practical implications Calibrated risk probabilities may support fraud-alert prioritization, risk ranking, threshold setting, and secondary review, helping institutions weigh predictive gains against computational cost. For LendingClub, the inclusion of loan grade and interest rate makes the framework more appropriate for post-pricing monitoring than for independent pre-pricing approval. Operational use would require institution-specific validation, monitoring for drift and subgroup performance, documented decision thresholds, and human oversight. Social implications The study integrates tabular attention, domain-specialized simulated quantum representations, calibration analysis and cost-aware optimization in one decision-support framework, while evaluating incremental value without claiming inherent quantum advantage. Originality/value The contribution is the theoretically motivated integration of tabular attention, domain-specialized simulated quantum representations, calibration analysis and cost-aware optimization in a unified financial decision-support framework. The study does not claim inherent quantum advantage; instead, it tests the incremental value of simulated quantum modules through temporal evaluation, strong nonhybrid comparisons and component-level ablations.

papers.title: Pembelajaran Neuroanatomi dalam Pendidikan Kedokteran: Tinjauan Naratif tentang Hambatan Belajar dan Media Pendukung
papers.abstract: Neuroanatomy challenges medical students to integrate spatial relationships, neural pathways, and clinical reasoning. This targeted literature review critically examines learning barriers and supporting instructional media. Fifteen primary studies published between 2018 and 2026 were synthesized narratively by theme; the selection stages were described with reference to PRISMA 2020, although complete search records were unavailable. Participants, study designs, interventions, outcomes, and limitations were compared across cognitive-curricular barriers, immersive spatial visualization, and physical or active learning. Reported neurophobia and conceptual difficulty were linked to perceived complexity and insufficient integration with clinical applications. However, interactivity did not consistently yield better performance. Randomized comparisons found no statistically significant advantage of immersive virtual reality over printed materials or of interactive modules over comparable reading materials. A separate comparative study favored physical brain cross-sections over augmented reality for the tasks assessed. Other studies suggested benefits from mixed reality, three-dimensional visualization, and flipped classrooms, but interpretation was constrained by small samples, short follow-up, or uncontrolled designs. The synthesis therefore distinguishes satisfaction, immediate test scores, delayed retention, and transfer to clinical reasoning. Instruction should combine anatomical specimens, task-specific visualization, active clinical practice, and repeated assessment; future studies should examine long-term retention and clinical transfer.

papers.title: Tuning molten pool dynamics and keyhole formation during laser powder bed fusion through laser beam shaping
papers.abstract: Keyhole porosity remains a critical barrier to broader adoption of laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) AM. The short lifespan and rapid dynamics of the molten pool pose significant challenges in probing pore formation mechanisms. To address these challenges, a high-fidelity thermo-fluid model was implemented that integrates laser-material interactions, vapor recoil, multiple reflections, and Marangoni effects. Simulations reveal keyhole pore formation follows a cycle of localized overheating, wall instability, and collapse, with subsequent bubble evolution—entrapment, coalescence, or surface escape—dictated by molten pool flow dynamics. By employing this model as a computational testbed, we evaluate a beam-shaping strategy to mitigate porosity and compare four distinct energy distributions: Gaussian, flat-top, longitudinal elliptical, and transverse elliptical (TE). The TE profile, with its major axis perpendicular to the scan direction, uniquely mitigates localized energy concentration and reduces detrimental multi‑reflections, thereby stabilizing the keyhole and reducing susceptibility to porosity under the studied conditions. Crucially, the results suggest pore susceptibility can be reduced with a modest decrease in volumetric melt rate, while the predicted solidification conditions may favor equiaxed-grain formation. This simulation-derived beam optimization framework provides fundamental qualitative insights and guidance for reducing susceptibility to keyhole pores in high-integrity, microstructurally tailored materials produced by PBF-LB.

papers.title: Photocrosslinkable dECM-Methacrylate Composite Hydrogel for Enhanced Chondrogenic Differentiation and Cartilage Regeneration
papers.abstract: Abstract Decellularized extracellular matrix (dECM) provides tissue-specific biochemical cues essential for cartilage regeneration, yet its application has been largely restricted to an auxiliary role due to the inability to directly form stable crosslinked networks. In this study, we developed a photocrosslinkable composite hydrogel by modifying dECM with methacrylate groups to obtain dECM-MA and incorporating poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA). Upon UV irradiation, these components form a stable, covalently co-crosslinked network. The resulting scaffold exhibited favorable 3D printability, optimized degradation kinetics, and robust mechanical behavior. Importantly, the incorporation of dECM-MA significantly enhanced BMSC viability, proliferation, and chondrogenic differentiation, resulting in an approximately 3-fold upregulation of cartilage-specific protein expression (Col II, SOX9, and ACAN). In a rat cartilage defect model, dECM-MA-rich scaffolds promoted superior hyaline-like cartilage regeneration and increased glycosaminoglycan deposition. Crucially, the regenerated tissue achieved a physiological weight-bearing compression modulus of approximately 10 MPa at 12 w while effectively suppressing fibrotic remodeling. These findings demonstrate that multiscale PEGDA/dECM-MA composite scaffolds with excellent mechanical properties and biocompatibility can be used for cartilage tissue engineering.

papers.title: Generalized Integral Transform-based Structural Damage Identification via Bayesian Parameter Estimation and Model Class Selection
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study presents a Bayesian framework for structural damage identification combining the Generalized Integral Transform Technique (GITT) with Bayesian parameter estimation and model class selection. Method The GITT is employed to obtain the time-domain structural response directly from the governing partial differential equations, avoiding the need for spatial discretization. The structural damage field is represented continuously in space through a Gaussian basis expansion, allowing the system integrity to be characterized by a reduced number of uncertain parameters compared to conventional finite element formulations. Bayesian inference is then used to estimate the posterior probability density functions of the uncertain parameters and to perform model class selection based on the computed evidences. The Transitional Markov Chain Monte Carlo method is adopted for efficient sampling and model evidence evaluation. Results Numerical investigations performed on an Euler–Bernoulli beam demonstrate the proposed method’s capability to detect, locate, and quantify damage under different scenarios and noise levels. Conclusion The results show that the proposed framework accurately identifies the true damage configuration, provides meaningful uncertainty quantification, and naturally penalizes overparameterized models, thus ensuring robust and physically consistent damage assessment.

papers.title: Design and comparison of custom cranial prostheses made of titanium and polyether ether ketone using the finite element method
papers.abstract: Abstract Cranioplasty is a surgical procedure for reconstructing cranial defects. This study compared the biomechanical performance of patient-specific cranial implants made of Ti6Al4V and PEEK using finite element analysis. A 3D model was reconstructed from CT data of a 19-year-old male with a right parietal defect. Static loads (50–400 N) were applied at three anatomical regions. PEEK implants exhibited higher von Mises stresses than titanium implants, while transferring more load to the surrounding bone. Stress concentration occurred in Region 3 under loads >200 N. Titanium provided greater protection to bone at the cost of stress shielding, whereas PEEK offered more physiological load sharing. Results highlight the importance of material selection based on defect location and expected loading conditions.

papers.title: Increased walking speed and reduced knee adduction moment following open-wedge high tibial osteotomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis of post-surgery gait biomechanics
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Open-wedge high tibial osteotomy (OWHTO) is an established treatment for younger and active patients with medial compartment knee osteoarthritis (OA). Although pain relief and radiographic correction are well documented, it remains unclear to what extent these improvements are accompanied by changes in gait function and medial knee joint loading. This meta-analysis evaluated changes in gait biomechanics following OWHTO, with particular emphasis on walking speed and the knee adduction moment (KAM), alongside changes in radiographic alignment and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). Methods Prospective and retrospective clinical studies evaluating gait before and after OWHTO were systematically reviewed. Within-patient changes in gait parameters, radiographic alignment, and PROMs were extracted and synthesized using a random effects meta-analysis; risk of bias was assessed with the ROBINS-I tool. Results Sixteen studies were included in the systematic review, of which fifteen, comprising 418 patients (460 knees), were included in the meta-analysis. Following OWHTO, walking speed significantly increased (mean difference [MD] 0.07 m/s, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.04 to 0.10) and maximum KAM significantly decreased (MD − 0.27 Nm/kg, 95% CI − 0.33 to − 0.21) compared with pre-surgery values. These biomechanical improvements were accompanied by correction of lower-limb alignment and improvement in most PROMs. Conclusions OWHTO is followed by an increase in walking speed and a reduction in KAM as a surrogate of medial compartment loading, alongside correction of lower-limb alignment and improvement in PROMs. As all included studies were uncontrolled pre-post comparisons, these findings describe changes following surgery rather than a causal treatment effect, and the clinical relevance of the small increase in walking speed remains uncertain. Quantitative gait analysis may complement conventional clinical and radiographic assessment following OWHTO, although its association with, and prognostic value for, patient outcomes remain to be established in future studies.

papers.title: How early-career researchers in health data science learn: a qualitative content analysis of learning strategies and teaching approaches
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Early career researchers in Health Data Science (HDS) struggle to effectively manage their learning process due to the novel and interdisciplinary nature of this field. To date, there is limited understanding about learning strategies in health data science. Therefore, we aim to uncover learning strategies that early career researchers employ to address their educational challenges, as well as shed light on their preferences regarding HDS teaching approach and course design. Method In this study, we conducted an inductive qualitative content analysis through semi-structured interviews with 10 early career researchers, including individuals pursuing master’s, PhD, and postdoctoral research programmes in HDS, across two institutions in the United Kingdom. Interviews were carried out in person from June 2023 to August 2023. Data were analysed qualitatively by inductive coding using NVivo software. Results Regarding learning strategies, we identified ten main categories with 22 codes, including collaboration, information seeking, active learning, focus granularity, elaboration, organisation, order granularity, goal orientation, reviewing, and deep learning strategies. Regarding course design and teaching, we discovered four categories with 14 codes, including course materials, duration and complexity, online discussion, and teaching approaches. Conclusions Early career researchers used a range of learning strategies aligned with available learning theories, such as peer learning, information seeking, and active learning. It is also evident that learners in HDS can favour interactive courses that provide them with hands-on experience and interactive discussion. The insights derived from our findings can enhance the quality of education in HDS.

papers.abstract: This article aims to formulate LITAK (Creative Question Circle) as a learning strategy designed to develop elementary school students’ questioning, expressing-opinion, and critical-thinking skills. The study employs a literature-based descriptive approach by examining relevant books and scholarly articles on active learning, questioning skills, inquiry learning, classroom discussion, and critical thinking in primary education. The reviewed literature indicates that student-generated questions can stimulate curiosity and initiate reasoning, while structured discussion provides opportunities to communicate ideas, listen to different perspectives, and provide reasons. Inquiry-oriented learning also encourages learners to examine information and draw conclusions rather than merely receive explanations. Based on these principles, LITAK is proposed as a cyclical classroom strategy consisting of orientation to a contextual stimulus, individual question formulation, question-circle sharing, peer response and reasoned argumentation, collaborative examination of information, and reflection with a conclusion. The teacher acts as a facilitator who ensures an inclusive atmosphere, guides the quality of questions, and helps students support their opinions with relevant evidence. The literature synthesis suggests that the integration of questioning, dialogue, and reasoning has pedagogical potential to support the three targeted competencies in an interconnected manner. However, this article presents a conceptual strategy developed from literature and does not report empirical classroom testing. Further research is required to assess its validity, practicality, and effectiveness in different elementary school contexts.

papers.title: Active learning in distance English language teaching
papers.abstract: Distance education is often judged by its pandemic-era performance and by the initial passivity of students. This critical narrative review addresses three questions: what made emergency remote teaching passive; what contemporary studies use to build engagement in distance education; and what this implies for teacher preparation and course design in English language teaching. Using targeted Boolean searches, thirteen peer-reviewed studies published between 2021 and 2026 were purposively selected from the Scopus database. Each study’s claims were critically appraised against its methodology, and the recommendations of the reviewed studies were ranked by practical usability and empirical strength. The evidence is more consistent with inadequate preparation and unadapted design than with the digital medium itself as the main source of passivity during emergency remote teaching. Contemporary tools such as text chat, virtual reality, and chatbots based on artificial intelligence help with active participation only when embedded in the structure of task sequencing, feedback, and teacher mediation. The evidence base remains uneven, often relying on small samples or self-reported data that combine compliance with genuine engagement. The findings shift attention from digital platforms to pedagogical design. To turn distance education into a setting for active language use without any passive access, the field should prioritise teacher preparation grounded in observed teaching practice, secure institutional support at the curriculum level and verify student engagement through more than satisfaction surveys alone. / Keywords: active learning, distance education, emergency remote teaching, English as a foreign language, student engagement, teacher preparation

papers.abstract: Abstract Amide bonds are prevalent in pharmaceuticals and bioactive compounds, yet traditional chemical synthesis relies on harsh conditions and generates stoichiometric waste. Biocatalysis offers a promising green approach. An acetyl-CoA synthetase from Methanocella arvoryzae (MethACS) was previously characterized for phenylalanine butylamide (FBA) production with poor performance. This study combined enzyme engineering and process intensification to enhance aqueous-phase FBA production. Guided by synergistic computational prediction and few-shot active learning, potential mutation sites were identified. The optimal mutant M450I/I546F was further obtained through greedy iterative combination, with 2.42-fold increased activity and prolonged half-life from 1.5 to 6.5 h at 60 °C. Then, the polyphosphate kinase 2-III (PPK2-III) and inorganic pyrophosphatase (PPI) were mined to construct a three-enzyme cascade for ATP regeneration and pyrophosphate (PPi) hydrolysis, resulting in a 5.52-fold increase in FBA concentration. Furthermore, the CipA-mediated self-assembly multienzyme cascade achieved the cyclic regeneration of ATP and a FBA yield of 2.34 g/L. Benefiting from system-level coordination, complete conversion of butyric acid was achieved with only a 2-fold excess amine substrate (previously required ≥4-fold excess), yielding an FBA titer of 2.34 g/L. This work provides a platform for green synthesis of high-value amides.

papers.abstract: This study examines the relationships between artificial intelligence (AI)-designed active learning and science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) students’ perceived course success in higher education mathematics and statistics courses. A correlational research design was utilized which included 330 undergraduate students undertaking mathematics and statistics courses. A 47-item questionnaire was developed to collect data, which were analyzed using exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The findings indicate that AI-designed active learning dimensions are strongly and positively correlated with students’ perceived success (PS) in mathematics and statistics courses. papers.title: Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nitride supported on a porous titanium mesh into adjacent pristine regions and dual‐defect microregions bearing cyano and nitrogen‐vacancy defects. Multiphysics simulations and potentiometric scanning electrochemical microscopy measurements suggest that this spatial architecture produces a localized potential response near the catalyst‐liquid interface, while in situ fluorescence microscopy indicates enhanced local O 2 availability. This coupled response is proposed to bridge the intrinsic timescale gap by facilitating directional extraction of photogenerated electrons while accelerating interfacial O 2 enrichment. The defect microregions promote proton‐coupled sequential two‐step O 2 reduction, whereas the conductive titanium mesh suppresses local electron accumulation and carbon nitride self‐photocorrosion. The optimized L‐CN/TM‐PS2 produces 2538 µmol L −1 g −1 H 2 O 2 within 120 min and achieves approximately 98.6% Escherichia coli inactivation. This work establishes the laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy as a design principle for synchronizing charge transport and mass transfer in supported photocatalysts for continuous‐flow environmental disinfection.

papers.title: Comparative study of fundamental mathematical competences in STEM learning: Objective, implications, and obstacles in Indonesia and Malaysia
papers.abstract: Indonesia and Malaysia both prioritize STEM education, offering a relevant context for comparing practices that support students’ fundamental mathematics competencies (FMC). This comparative study aims to examine and analyze the implementation of STEM in mathematics instruction in both countries, while also identifying the challenges faced by teachers. Furthermore, it explores how STEM practices relate to students' FMC and 21st-century skills, and assesses the extent to which the resulting models can be applied in other contexts. Four junior high schools (two per country) that had implemented STEM in mathematics were selected purposively, involving four mathematics teachers and 115 students (64 Indonesian, 51 Malaysian). Data were collected through video-recorded lesson observations, semi-structured teacher interviews, a Student Perceptions of Learning questionnaire, and an FMC test. Findings revealed that STEM practices in both countries were closely aligned, combining hands-on and minds-on activities, while teachers creatively compensated for limited infrastructure. Students in both countries reported positive perceptions of critical thinking, problem-solving, collaboration, and communication. Malaysian students showed greater gains in creativity, technology use, and collaboration, whereas Indonesian students were stronger in communication. Comparable FMC test performance suggests high potential for adopting, adapting, and validating the pedagogical model across countries. STEM integration facilitated active learning and deeper conceptual understanding of mathematics.

papers.title: A diffusion world model and multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for predictive routing in healthcare IoT
papers.abstract: Abstract Healthcare Internet of Things (H-IoT) networks support monitoring through wearable sensors, implantable devices, bedside units, mobile gateways, edge nodes, and cloud platforms. Reliable routing is challenging as medical packets are delay-sensitive, while networks face limited energy, mobility, lossy links, congestion, traffic bursts, and sudden node or link failures. This paper presents a diffusion world model and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for predictive H-IoT routing. The proposed design models the network as a dynamic graph, uses a Temporal Graph Transformer (TGT) to model spatial-temporal dependencies, forecasts link stability, congestion, and failure risk, and uses decentralized agents to select next hops. In ten paired, pre-configured software-emulation scenarios, the executable routing reference prototype achieved measured mean packet delivery ratio of $$56.24\pm 4.75\%$$ , delay of $$42.79\pm 3.34$$ ms, application goodput of $$6.11\pm 0.51$$ kbps, repair overhead of $$0.151\pm 0.024$$ , sensor-radio energy of $$8.94\pm 0.02$$ J, recovery time of $$0.0297\pm 0.0005$$ s, and restricted mean time to first sensor death of $$272.5\pm 44.9$$ s. Source-informed baseline adaptations achieved higher delivery and goodput and lower delay, while the prototype recovered successful routes faster. A separate 20-seed federated-predictor benchmark on emulated patient-group data reported patient-level DP-SGD accountant bound $$(\epsilon ,\delta )=(8,10^{-5})$$ . DP-FedAvg with rehearsal achieved task-1 and task-2 accuracies of $$72.26\pm 1.06\%$$ and $$70.16\pm 0.94\%$$ , respectively, with $$2.24\pm 0.84$$ percentage points of task-1 forgetting.

papers.title: Surface-state-driven post-processing framework for additively manufactured titanium tubes using sustainable magnetorheological finishing
papers.abstract: Purpose Additive manufacturing of titanium alloys enables intricate part designs, yet this comes at the cost of poor surface quality, characterized by stair-step artifacts, partially fused particles and high roughness, which ultimately limits their practical applicability. This study aims to propose a surface-state-driven post-processing framework using sustainable magnetorheological polishing (S-MRP) to address AM-induced surface defects while preserving process sustainability. Design/methodology/approach Selective laser melting (SLM) was used to fabricate Ti6Al4V titanium alloy microtubes using powder feedstock with an average particle size of 50 µm. A novel eco-friendly Sustainable Magnetorheological Polishing (S-MRP) fluid was subsequently developed and applied as a mechanical, rheology-based surface finishing technique for post-processing the additively manufactured specimens. The study establishes explicit correlations among SLM-fabricated surface characteristics, magnetorheological fluid behaviour and material removal mechanisms, thereby enabling controlled mechanical shear-based finishing without inducing thermal or chemical surface alterations. A response surface methodology (RSM) is used to optimize the interactive effects of tool rotation, workpiece rotation and tool reciprocation on surface evolution. The sustainability of the process is evaluated through life cycle assessment, comparing the developed fluid with a conventional formulation. Findings Results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables deterministic surface-state transformation, reducing surface roughness from 2.4 to 0.28 µm (87 % improvement), while ensuring uniform defect removal and significantly improved surface morphology, reduced surface roughness and establishing a controlled surface-state transformation suitable for subsequent functional applications. The S-MRP fluid exhibits improved rheological stability, magnetic responsiveness and reduced sedimentation, contributing to consistent finishing performance. In addition, a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment confirms that the sustainable formulation reduces global warming potential and fossil resource consumption compared to conventional fluids. Originality/value This study advances additive manufacturing (AM) post-processing by integrating surface engineering, process optimization and sustainability, thereby offering a scalable pathway to enhance the functional performance of AM components. The proposed process significantly improves the surface quality of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V tubes and provides a promising post-processing strategy for components intended for demanding engineering applications. Application-specific qualification, however, requires further investigation.

papers.title: Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nitride supported on a porous titanium mesh into adjacent pristine regions and dual‐defect microregions bearing cyano and nitrogen‐vacancy defects. Multiphysics simulations and potentiometric scanning electrochemical microscopy measurements suggest that this spatial architecture produces a localized potential response near the catalyst‐liquid interface, while in situ fluorescence microscopy indicates enhanced local O 2 availability. This coupled response is proposed to bridge the intrinsic timescale gap by facilitating directional extraction of photogenerated electrons while accelerating interfacial O 2 enrichment. The defect microregions promote proton‐coupled sequential two‐step O 2 reduction, whereas the conductive titanium mesh suppresses local electron accumulation and carbon nitride self‐photocorrosion. The optimized L‐CN/TM‐PS2 produces 2538 µmol L −1 g −1 H 2 O 2 within 120 min and achieves approximately 98.6% Escherichia coli inactivation. This work establishes the laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy as a design principle for synchronizing charge transport and mass transfer in supported photocatalysts for continuous‐flow environmental disinfection.

papers.title: Advanced drug delivery strategies for overcoming tumor-mediated molecular hijacking: Emerging nanotherapeutics, advanced biotherapeutics, and artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in precision oncology fueled the development of nanotherapeutics,​ molecularly targeted drugs, engineered immunotherapies, RNA therapeutics, and smart biomaterials for more selective cancer treatment. However, long-term therapeutic responses remain restricted by interconnected adaptive mechanisms, including ABC transporter-mediated drug efflux, dysregulated signaling pathways, apoptosis evasion, immune escape, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and tumor microenvironment​ remodeling. In this review article, these processes are collectively framed as tumor-mediated molecular hijacking, describing malignant cell exploitation and microenvironmental pathways that promote multidrug resistance and therapeutic failure. The review critically examines nanotherapeutic and advanced biotherapeutic strategies to counteract these mechanisms, including functionalized nanocarriers, antibody-drug conjugates, CAR-T cells, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy, immune checkpoint blockade, mesenchymal stem-cell (MSC)-based therapeutics, CRISPR-mediated genome editing, bispecific T-cell engagers, and RNA-based approaches. Particular focus includes drug-delivery elements such as tumour penetration, intracellular trafficking, controlled release, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, and critical formulation attributes, as well as translational challenges such as manufacturability, scalability, reproducibility, stability, safety, and regulatory feasibility. Emerging biofabrication approaches enable the fabrication of adaptive and personalized delivery systems, while artificial intelligence and machine learning are utilized as tools for structure-guided design, nanocarrier optimization, treatment-response prediction, and patient-specific digital-twin modelling. This paper combines tumor-mediated molecular hijacking with drug delivery technology at the forefront and translational aspects to create a comprehensive platform for clinically relevant precision cancer therapeutics.Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

papers.title: Avances en las técnicas de cirugía plástica reconstructiva para el tratamiento de defectos complejos de tejidos blandos. Revisión sistematica
papers.abstract: Introducción: Los defectos complejos de tejidos blandos, caracterizados por la pérdida de cobertura cutánea, volumen y estructuras de soporte, representan un desafío reconstructivo de alta complejidad. Esta revisión sistemática tiene como pregunta guía: ¿cuáles son los avances en las técnicas de cirugía plástica reconstructiva para el tratamiento de defectos complejos de tejidos blandos y qué evidencia respalda su efectividad? Métodos: Se siguió la declaración PRISMA 2020. Se realizaron búsquedas en PubMed, Scopus y Web of Science con términos como complex soft tissue defects, reconstructive plastic surgery, perforator flaps, free flap, skin substitutes y 3D bioprinting, limitando a publicaciones entre 2023 y 2025. Se incluyeron estudios primarios, revisiones sistemáticas, revisiones narrativas y artículos técnicos en inglés y español que abordaran técnicas reconstructivas de tejidos blandos; se excluyeron estudios con población o intervención no pertinentes y publicaciones sin texto completo disponible. Resultados: Se identificaron 342 registros, de los cuales, tras eliminar duplicados y aplicar los criterios de elegibilidad, se incluyeron 26 fuentes. La evidencia se agrupó en cinco ejes: colgajos perforantes y microcirugía, reconstrucción de extremidades y abordaje ortoplástico, sustitutos cutáneos e ingeniería de tejidos, bioimpresión 3D y medicina regenerativa, y reconstrucción de defectos volumétricos complejos. Los hallazgos muestran una transición desde técnicas tradicionales hacia estrategias personalizadas que combinan colgajos perforantes, sustitutos dérmicos y constructos bioingenierizados. Conclusiones: Los avances en colgajos perforantes, sustitutos cutáneos y bioimpresión 3D amplían el arsenal reconstructivo; sin embargo, la evidencia comparativa prospectiva sigue siendo limitada. Se requieren estudios con desenlaces estandarizados que permitan definir algoritmos de selección técnica y consolidar protocolos reproducibles.

papers.title: Architecture of a virtual simulation teaching platform designed for college students' innovation and entrepreneurship training and its empirical study
papers.abstract: Innovation and entrepreneurship education requires experiential and adaptive learning environments, but evidence is often limited by weak theoretical integration, incomplete intervention reporting, and non-randomized designs. This study evaluated a theory-informed virtual simulation platform for entrepreneurial learning while explicitly accounting for allocation, instructional exposure, measurement quality, and clustering. A two-arm quasi-experimental study included 480 students from 12 intact classes. Baseline assessment preceded non-random classroom allocation to the virtual simulation platform (six classes; n = 240) or conventional training (six classes; n = 240); students did not self-select. Two instructors taught both conditions using common objectives, schedules, and assessment tasks over eight weeks. Multi-item measures underwent reliability and confirmatory factor analysis, performance tasks were scored by blinded independent raters, and primary analyses used covariate-adjusted ANCOVA with classroom-, instructor-, exposure-, missing-data-, and alternative-composite sensitivity analyses. Baseline characteristics were comparable, although post-allocation attendance, active learning time, assignment completion, and participation were higher in the platform condition. Platform assignment was associated with a 6.96-point higher composite learning score (95% CI: 6.34–7.57, p < 0.001); the estimate remained 5.38 points (95% CI: 4.69–6.07) after exploratory adjustment for observed instructional exposure. Classroom-clustered and instructor-adjusted models were consistent. Engagement was the only significant specific indirect pathway, but it explained only 5.41% of the total association. Scale reliability, construct validity, and inter-rater reliability were acceptable to strong. The findings provide supportive, but not definitive causal, evidence that a structured virtual simulation environment is associated with better entrepreneurial learning, engagement, and acceptability. The magnitude of benefit should be interpreted alongside exposure differences, possible novelty and Hawthorne effects, assessment alignment, classroom clustering, and the single-institution context.

papers.title: Bridging Policy and Practice in Competency-Based Islamic History Education: Multi-Phase Alignment and Pedagogical Reconstruction
papers.abstract: This study investigates the vertical alignment and pedagogical translation of competency-based curricula across developmental phases, addressing the critical research gap between normative policy mandates and actual classroom enactment. Employing a qualitative document analysis and policy-practice synthesis, we evaluated a targeted corpus of national policy directives (Capaian Pembelajaran) alongside peer-reviewed empirical evaluations (2020–2026) using Bloom and Marzano's cognitive taxonomies. The analysis reveals a profound, systemic policy-practice gap across three dimensions: a cognitive mismatch between mandated higher-order thinking and entrenched rote-memorization, pedagogical barriers due to teacher-centered transmission, and assessment inertia. While the policy outlines a progressive, multi-phase cognitive continuum—transitioning from lower-secondary dynastic narratives to upper-secondary global civilizational synthesis—actual instruction remains decoupled from these standards. To resolve this, we propose a reconstructed pedagogical framework that structurally aligns instructional models with curriculum phases, prioritizing Project-Based Learning (PjBL) for digital artifact creation in lower-secondary levels and Problem-Based Learning (PBL) for historical inquiry in upper-secondary levels. This study advances curriculum scholarship by offering a replicable, phase-aligned model for religious humanities education, demonstrating how structured active learning can bridge universal policy-practice divides in global competency-based reforms

papers.title: Pengembangan E-Modul Fisika Berbasis Inkuiri Terbimbing Terintegrasi Green Physics Pada Peserta Didik SMA
papers.abstract: Physics instruction in senior high schools remains largely teacher-centered, while renewable energy topics are difficult to visualize due to limited laboratory equipment, leaving students' science process skills underdeveloped. This study aimed to develop a guided inquiry-based physics e-module integrated with green physics principles on renewable energy to enhance the science process skills of tenth-grade students. The study employed a Research and Development approach using the Rowntree model, comprising planning, development, and evaluation stages, combined with Tessmer's formative evaluation involving self evaluation, expert review, one-to-one evaluation, and small group evaluation. A field trial was conducted with 33 tenth-grade students at SMA Negeri 3 Banyuasin 1 using a pretest-posttest design. The results showed that the e-module achieved a validity score of 88.4% (Highly Valid) and a practicality score of 87.9% (Highly Practical). N-Gain analysis revealed an increase in science process skills of 0.65 (moderate category), with average scores rising from 33.9 to 77.0. These findings indicate that the developed e-module is feasible as an alternative physics learning medium that integrates conceptual mastery with environmental awareness, while supporting the implementation of active learning under the Kurikulum Merdeka.

papers.title: POWER-LET: Physics-Informed Optimal Transport for Cross-Domain Radiation Risk Modelling Between Terrestrial Electromagnetic Fields and Space Radiation
papers.abstract: The biological effects of radiation depend on the underlying mechanism of energy transfer. Ionising radiation produces direct molecular damage, whereas the biological effects of extremely low-frequency electromagnetic fields (ELF-EMF) remain uncertain and are generally associated with indirect cellular responses. This study presents a computational framework for comparing the biological effects of terrestrial ELF-EMF and ionising space radiation. A literature-informed correlation matrix was developed to compare four radiation environments: electrical substation ELF-EMF, Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR), Solar Particle Events (SPE), and trapped radiation belts. Four biological endpoints were considered, namely DNA double-strand breaks, oxidative stress, membrane permeability damage, and chromosomal aberrations. The comparison shows consistently stronger associations between ionising radiation and biological damage than between ELF-EMF and the same endpoints. An Advanced Radiation Simulator Suite was developed to quantify radiation effects in both terrestrial and space environments. The terrestrial model incorporates electromagnetic field attenuation and exposure modelling. The space radiation model combines radiation shielding with established radiobiological dose-response models. The study also introduces the POWER-LET (Power-network Optimal Wasserstein Embedding for Radiation-Linear Energy Transfer) framework. The framework constructs a shared latent space between terrestrial EMF and space radiation descriptors using Optimal Transport. Physics-informed constraints are incorporated to ensure consistency with established physical laws. Uncertainty quantification is included to evaluate the reliability of cross-domain predictions. The simulation results demonstrate a clear separation between ionising and non-ionising radiation environments while preserving physically meaningful relationships within the latent representation. The uncertainty analysis provides a transparent assessment of prediction confidence for cross-domain mapping. The proposed framework offers an integrated approach for comparative radiation assessment and provides a foundation for future studies in radiation biology, space medicine, radiation protection, and electrical power systems.

papers.title: Mapping the Paradigm Shift in Natural Science Education: A Structural Analysis of Problem-Based Learning and Socio-scientific Reasoning (2016–2026)
papers.abstract: The escalating complexity of global socioscientific issues demands an urgent paradigm shift in natural science education toward frameworks that rigorously cultivate higher-order socioscientific reasoning. However, while problem-based learning (PBL) is widely applied, the literature remains fragmented, creating a pedagogical bottleneck that obscures clear pathways for structural instructional design. This study analyzes the research trajectory of critical thinking and PBL using a bibliometric analysis combined with a systematic literature review (SLR) based on the PRISMA protocol. Data from the Scopus database (2016–2026) yielded 99 eligible articles from an initial 433. The structural mapping reveals a paradigm shift from basic evaluation toward targeted problem-solving, with publications peaking in 2025 (29 articles) and driven prominently by contributors from the United States and Indonesia within core journals like Advances in Physiology Education. VOSviewer analysis identified three precise conceptual nodes: evidence-based pedagogical assessment, active learning implementation, and the conceptual nexus of PBL and critical thinking. The SLR synthesis indicates that PBL enhances these competencies specifically by scaffolding collaborative scientific inquiry and integrating blended active learning environments. Ultimately, these findings dictate that future instructional models must evolve beyond traditional boundaries, utilizing these structural nodes to design adaptive, technology-integrated curricula that effectively operationalize socioscientific reasoning.

papers.title: Mesoscale Neural Operators: Learning Nonlinear Constitutive Laws from Molecular Dynamics for Scalable Fracture Predictions
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can capture the nanoscale physics of fracture at the atomistic level, but their computational cost prohibits predictions at the length scales and time scales needed for many applications. Machine learning approaches, on the other hand, have been proposed as heuristic surrogates for material fracture, yet they cannot guarantee the physical consistency of the predicted response. To address this shortcoming, we propose the mesoscale neural operator (MNO): a data-driven nonlocal constitutive model that is learned directly from MD loading and displacement data. After training, it can be used in continuum fracture simulations on much larger domains and grid sizes. The key idea of the MNO is to exploit the built-in characteristic length of a nonlocal model, called the horizon, to travel across scales. Physical consistency across scales is obtained by building two structural ingredients into the MNO: a normalized kernel that renders the strain energy density invariant under horizon rescaling, and a rescaled critical bond stretch that keeps the energy release rate consistent across scales. Through tests on synthetic data, we show that the MNO and its learning workflow indeed discover the nonlocal continuum multiscale model in the form of the nonlocal kernel and the nonlinear constitutive relation. We then apply the framework to coarse-grained MD data and find that in a test problem, the learned model matches the MD strain energy density and critical energy release rate within 3%. It also predicts the peak transmitted forces within 6% in out-of-distribution tension tests. As a further demonstration, the model is applied to a plate with 4000 times the area of the training specimens and containing an initial defect. In this problem, the model reproduces the main features of dynamic brittle fracture, including branch and cascading branch networks.

papers.title: Toward Planning Representations That Separate Task Structure from Visual Content
papers.abstract: Effective planning requires representations that preserve task-relevant geometry and object identity while ignoring visual variation that does not alter the task. Existing evaluations of visual generalization often change several factors simultaneously, making the source of a failure difficult to identify. We introduce a controlled evaluation of object-goal navigation (ObjectNav), the task of reaching an instance of a named object category, in procedurally generated ProcTHOR houses. Training and evaluation houses share floor plans, object locations, goals, and start states, while visual factors are changed individually or in combination. Across model-free reinforcement learning (RL), model-based RL, and agents using frozen pretrained visual representations, our results show that appearance changes impair navigation, but their effects differ sharply by factor. Surface material changes account for most of the average change in success, whereas clutter and lighting have little effect. The magnitude of a global image statistics shift does not reliably predict performance: changing only the goal object's appearance can substantially impair an end-to-end agent despite a small image-level change. We found that a model based agent that plans over frozen features from the pretrained DINOv2 image encoder achieves the highest success (0.83) under the full shift, but remains sensitive to surface appearance. Our experiments reveal an important requirement for planning representations: they must separate invariant spatial task structure from appearance.

papers.title: NAP-Wave: A Neural Adaptive Plane-Wave Architecture for High-Frequency Helmholtz Problems
papers.abstract: Training neural networks to simulate highly oscillatory wavefields presents optimization challenges, often hindered by spectral bias and poorly conditioned physics-based loss landscapes. To address these challenges and enhance convergence, we propose NAP-Wave, a joint neural architecture and training strategy that expands the target scattered wavefield in an adaptive neural plane-wave basis. The basis functions are extracted from all hidden layers and modulated by trainable plane-wave carriers, embedding the high-frequency oscillatory physics directly into the network's trial space. NAP-Wave is trained on a physics-informed loss built from the Lippmann-Schwinger integral equation, so no differentiation of the network with respect to its input is required. We develop a decoupled optimization strategy in which Adam updates the parameters of the neural plane-wave basis, while the linear combination coefficients are computed exactly by a least-squares (LS) solver. We couple this with an adaptive-depth training strategy in which the network starts shallow and grows progressively layer-by-layer. At each growth step, we avoid the loss spikes typical of dynamic network growth using the LS-computed coefficients, the warm-started parameters, and the preservation of the first- and second-order optimizer moments of the previous stage. Ablation studies confirm that the plane-wave basis, the exact coefficient solve, and the progressive schedule independently accelerate convergence and improve accuracy. Validated on exact-solution benchmarks, NAP-Wave achieves relative L2 errors of order 1%. On highly heterogeneous geophysical benchmarks, it achieves relative errors of 5%, 9%, and 10%, significantly outperforming published PINN methods in both accuracy and convergence time. To ensure reproducibility, the code is available at https://github.com/Hamza-Kamil/NAP-WAVE.

papers.title: Representing Differential Inclusions as Monads: A Framework for Compositional Controller Synthesis
papers.abstract: Sequential composition of safety-certified controllers for hybrid and non-smooth robotic systems is well studied piecewise. Yet no existing framework reduces this question to a single algebraic condition. We construct a \emph{trajectory monad} for Filippov-regular differential inclusions. Its Kleisli category treats controllers as morphisms and sequential execution as trajectory concatenation. Control Barrier Function (CBF) certification, a guarantee of forward invariance, corresponds to a sub-monad of this category. Joint safety of composed controllers then follows from one algebraic condition. All controllers must land in a common sub-monad, which is closed under the monad multiplication.   The sub-monad condition recasts recasts existing CBF composition practice categorically. It explains why a smooth intersection of multiple barriers supports safe composition, while enforcing barriers phase by phase does not. For the phase-by-phase case, we derive a closed-form Bernoulli model of the failure rate. We validate it over a randomized sweep of 3{,}000 instances. The same sweep shows that the standard baseline degrades under constraint conflict as the barrier count grows. This baseline enforces all barriers simultaneously as constraints in a single quadratic program (QP). We instantiate the framework on a four-mode piecewise-affine system and on a unicycle reduced-order model over heterogeneous terrain.

papers.title: Successive Convexification in Learned World Models for Safe Offline Planning
papers.abstract: World models learned from offline data allow an agent to plan without further interaction with the environment, but the sampling-based planners used with them handle safety constraints only by scoring or rejecting sampled action sequences. We instead pose safe planning in the latent space of a learned world model as a successive convex program (SCP), in which a learned discrete-time control barrier function is imposed as a constraint at every step of the horizon. SCP requires smooth dynamics, so we build the networks from smoothed MaxMin activations and spectrally normalised layers, and bound the resulting linearisation error in terms of the Lipschitz bound and the smoothing width. As SCP is a local method, we start it from a sampled plan. On two Safety-Gymnasium navigation tasks with offline data, this planner has fewer violations than MPPI and CEM drawing 128 times as many samples at equal wall-clock time in our main comparison, though not significantly, and earns greater return at longer horizons, and is much safer than SCP without a sampled start. SCP converged more often on Lipschitz-bounded models. Unlike sampling, it also reports at each step whether its plan is a feasible, first-order optimal KKT point of the planning problem in the model, or that no feasible plan was found nearby. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/youngers2006/scwm.

papers.title: PopulationBalanceModels.jl: An Extensible Framework for Deploying Population Balance Models
papers.abstract: Population balance models (PBMs) are used to describe a diverse range of processes that have a distribution over one or more intrinsic properties. However, implementing PBMs for a new application often requires developing and verifying application-specific code for numerical solution and analysis. In this work, we present PopulationBalanceModels.jl, an open-source Julia package designed to make PBMs easy to implement. Users construct models from individual physical terms and select the numerical methods separately. Common solver and observation interfaces allow the same model to be used for simulation, Bayesian parameter estimation, and uncertainty quantification. The package currently supports various model types such as coupled and/or multi-dimensional PBMs, coupling of a PBM to a bulk mass/energy balance, and transport in an axially-dispersed plug flow reactor. While a broad range of physical terms and corresponding numerical methods are already implemented, the package is designed to support extensibility in both aspects, enabling users to incorporate new mechanisms and numerical methods into existing workflows.

papers.title: Enforcing Ellipsoidal Constraints in Neural Networks with a Polynomial Safety Layer
papers.abstract: Often the output of a learned mapping must satisfy prescribed constraints. In the control of autonomous systems, for example, the chosen action must keep the system within a collision-free region. We consider the case in which a proposed output is corrected by projection onto a safety ellipsoid. Computing this projection amounts to solving a quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP). We construct a neural-network safety layer by unrolling a feasibility-preserving polynomial penalty iteration. The unrolled structure allows the loss gradient to propagate from the feasible output through the safety layer to the network parameters during training. We show how to choose the layer parameters so that every iterate is feasible and give a computable bound on its distance to the exact projection at any prescribed depth. We illustrate the method by training a LiDAR-based policy to control an unmanned aerial vehicle. A privileged model predictive control expert uses the map and the measured vehicle state to generate the training data. In the simulated narrow mazes, the filtered policy avoided wall contact at every tested stage of training, including at initialization, when every unfiltered flight hit a wall. A representative build of the learned policy and its safety layer for an Arm Cortex-M4F microcontroller occupies about 36 KiB of flash, with a RAM budget below 5 KiB.

papers.title: Gradient-Based Co-Design of Systems and Reinforcement Learning Policies with Differentiable Simulators
papers.abstract: Co-design is the problem of jointly optimizing the design of a system and the policy that operates it. Neither can be chosen independently: a system design is only as good as the policy trained for it, and the optimal policy changes with the design. When that policy is learned by reinforcement learning (RL), evaluating a candidate design requires a full policy training run, and the design is usually optimized by black-box search such as Bayesian optimization (BO) or evolution strategies (ES). These methods scale poorly with the design dimension and ignore the differentiable structure of modern simulators and, in particular, the sensitivity of the optimal policy with respect to the design. We instead derive a gradient-based co-design method, where the design gradient decomposes into a direct effect of changing the design at a fixed policy and an indirect effect through the design-dependent optimal policy. The indirect effect requires the sensitivity of the converged policy to the design, which we obtain by applying the implicit function theorem to the stationarity condition of the policy gradient. Based on this sensitivity, we develop a proof-of-concept co-design algorithm with stochastic value gradient (SVG)-style policy optimization, prove that it converges to an approximately stationary design, and demonstrate on a differentiable networked-system benchmark with high-dimensional design spaces that it consistently outperforms BO and ES.

papers.title: Residual Reinforcement Learning for Visual Servo Control with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer
papers.abstract: We address tracking a moving object on a conveyor with a Franka Emika Panda robot arm, despite an imprecise digital twin, measurement errors, and noise. Our novel approach augments a loop-shaped inverse-Jacobian PI controller with a residual policy learned via Soft Actor-Critic in the digital twin. A delay-compensated Kalman filter fuses out-of-sequence camera measurements to provide latency-aware moving target position estimates. We compare the achieved performance to a performance bound for a class of model-based controllers derived from a frequency-domain sensitivity analysis, quantifying the minimum achievable error imposed by uncertain kinematic model mismatch. Simulation and hardware experiments indicate that our residual policy drives tracking error below the bound. Across conveyor speeds (27.9-41.8 mm/s), our method reduces mean tracking errors from 1.1-1.4 mm (baseline inverse-Jacobian PI) to 0.3-0.7 mm. These results show that learning residual corrections in a limited-fidelity simulator, combined with delay compensation, can substantially improve model-based control under modeling and measurement uncertainties while maintaining reliable sim-to-real transfer.

papers.title: STaSBO: LLM-Guided Strategy Planning and Configuration Selection for Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) enables sample-efficient search for expensive black-box problems, but its performance depends strongly on surrogate-acquisition configurations whose suitability varies across problems and optimization states. STaSBO comprises two coordinated stages: strategy planning and strategy-guided configuration selection. papers.title: Learning inadequacy of Bayesian neural operators for PDE-constrained inference and design
papers.abstract: Partial differential equations (PDEs) underpin predictive modeling across science, engineering and medicine. Their use in digital twins, parameter inference and optimal design requires repeated solutions across parameters and scenarios. For nonlinear, transient and multiphysics systems, these calculations can make numerical simulation prohibitively expensive. Here we introduce the residual-informed Bayesian neural operator (RI-BNO), which learns operator inadequacy using a posteriori error estimates from the governing PDEs and incorporates its correction and uncertainty into Bayesian training and prediction. We establish local error bounds for the residual-informed estimates under stability and smoothness assumptions. We demonstrate RI-BNO on a non-linear reaction-diffusion benchmark with DeepONet and latent-subspace architectures, Markov chain Monte Carlo inference of glioma parameter fields from magnetic resonance imaging, and Monte Carlo risk-averse optimization of three-dimensional thermal breaks in building envelopes under manufacturing uncertainty. Across the evaluated examples, RI-BNO improves agreement with finite element (FE) reference predictions, parameter posteriors and optimized designs while using half as many full nonlinear or transient training simulations as the vanilla Bayesian neural operator (vBNO). For thermal break design, online optimization time decreases from 178 hours with the FE model to 18 minutes with RI-BNO. These results demonstrate the value of explicit inadequacy modeling in neural operators for reliable PDE-based inference and design.

papers.title: Leaning Over to Reach Far-Away Objects
papers.abstract: We study supported reaching to extend a humanoid robot's workspace by bracing against the environment for stabilization using a straightforward yet capable whole-body model predictive control (MPC) approach, exclusively with local sensing and fiducial markers. While typical solutions for whole body humanoid control aim at avoiding or accommodating contact, contact is explicitly required to reach objects placed on surfaces far out of normal reach. We employ sampling-based MPC for whole-body leaning, bracing, reaching, and recovery on a Unitree H1-2 humanoid. The controller runs in real-time at 34 Hz on a laptop, transfers sim-to-real, extends reach by about 50 cm beyond the unbraced standing workspace, and sustains the loaded posture for over four minutes, before pose estimation drifts. The controller reaches the commanded target in 89% of trials and completes the full reach-and-recovery cycle in 81%, across 54 trials spanning six targets and three table heights. We further characterize why such a small real-time sampling budget is sufficient, finding that temporal persistence of sampled actions and exploration scale strongly govern success, while CEM provides the widest operating region over planning rate and model mismatch. These results establish a real-world baseline for online, contact-rich humanoid manipulation. Code, videos, and full hardware details are available at https://h12leaner.github.io/

papers.title: Voyage-level energy management of wind-assisted ships with controllable pitch propellers under realistic metocean conditions
papers.abstract: Wind-assisted propulsion introduces route-dependent renewable wind energy into ship propulsion, but its fuel-saving benefit depends on the coupled response of sail thrust, propeller loading, and engine efficiency under realistic metocean condition. This study develops a voyage-level energy management framework for wind-assisted ships equipped with controllable pitch propellers. The rigid wing sail orientation and propeller pitch setting are treated as coordinated operating variables, and a semi-empirical four-degree-of-freedom integrated ship energy performance model is combined with Bayesian optimization to minimize fuel consumption. Reynolds number-dependent sail aerodynamics and pitch-dependent controllable pitch propeller characteristics are integrated to represent wind-assisted thrust and propulsion system flexibility. Ten real-world voyages of a Kamsarmax bulk carrier are used to evaluate route-dependent energy saving performance. Propulsion-only optimization reduces fuel consumption by 0.50%–1.77%, sail-only optimization by 2.19%–9.23%, and joint sail–propulsion optimization by 3.17%–9.88%. The results show that wind-assisted thrust changes net propeller loading and engine operating points, making coordinated sail–propulsion energy management essential for realizing voyage-level fuel and emission reductions.

This narrative review discusses established applications, current limitations, and emerging research directions for 3D printing in Oto-HNS.

papers.title: Cradle-to-Gate Energy of Laser Powder Bed Fusion for Aerospace Titanium, Aluminium, and Magnesium Alloys: A Review
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) is routinely presented as a sustainable alternative to conventional aerospace manufacturing, but its energy advantage is conditional and alloy-specific. We review the material and energy chain of Ti-6Al-4V, AlSi10Mg, Scalmalloy, WE43, and AZ91 and compare the cradle-to-gate primary energy of each with the conventional route it displaces. For titanium, the collapse of the buy-to-fly (BTF) ratio cuts primary energy by approximately 62% at a conventional BTF of 8:1 (49 to 72% when build specific energy consumption, SEC, and feedstock inventory vary together); machining-chip recycling narrows the saving. For aluminium, the case holds only for machining-intensive parts; measured industrial build energies support it, laboratory ones can eliminate or reverse it. For magnesium, published data show no cradle-to-gate advantage: casting already operates close to net shape, so Mg L-PBF must be justified on geometric or functional grounds. This conclusion rests on estimated build SEC; metered electricity SEC below about 33 to 39 MJ/kg against a 2:1 casting baseline, or 124 to 130 MJ/kg at 3:1, would reverse it. The evidence base is markedly asymmetric; titanium has been investigated in many independent reuse studies, but results for magnesium are described in a single WE43 study with no cycle-resolved AZ91 data.

Previous studies tend to focus on a single model, medium, grade level, or school context, and existing reviews have not synthesized learning motivation specifically in elementary social studies. This study aimed to synthesize previous research on elementary school students' learning motivation in social studies. A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Articles published between January 2021 and February 2026 were searched in Google Scholar using Indonesian and English keywords. Of the 31 records identified, 22 were excluded at screening, nine reports were sought for retrieval, two could not be retrieved, and seven articles that met the criteria were analyzed using narrative and thematic synthesis. The findings show that learning motivation is shaped by three groups of factors: learning media (audio-visual media, augmented reality, and educational games), instructional models and strategies (such as Quantum Teaching Learning), and the teacher's role through reinforcement, varied teaching methods, and a personal approach. Motivation was also positively and significantly related to social studies learning outcomes. These findings suggest that teachers can sustain students' motivation by combining engaging media, active learning strategies, and consistent motivational support.

papers.abstract: A person’s dentition is a unique feature, and this variability has driven a shift toward customization in dentistry, where orthodontic treatment spans extended periods with constantly visible appliances. This review evaluates Selective Laser Melting (SLM) and Metal Injection Molding (MIM) as two manufacturing routes for metallic orthodontic brackets, each suited to different production requirements. This narrative review was conducted through searches of Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect, drawing on literature published between 1993 and 2026. Studies directly relevant to metallic orthodontic bracket manufacturing were prioritized, while related manufacturing studies were considered where bracket-specific evidence was limited. The review evaluates key manufacturing outcomes, including density, shrinkage, geometrical distortion, surface roughness, and mechanical properties, together with their clinical implications and commercial evidence. Both require post-processing, although heat treatment can significantly alter SLM surface roughness and geometrical stability. The evidence indicates process-level differences between SLM and MIM, although the magnitude of reported differences may also reflect factors such as material, geometry, and processing conditions. A key contribution of this review is a cluster-based framework for SLM process parameters, representing inputs, behaviors, phenomena, and outcomes as an interconnected system rather than independent variables, clarifying process complexity and its influence on part quality. MIM remains preferred for standardization, while SLM offers advantages in customization with the potential to improve treatment efficiency.

papers.abstract: Aim: This prospective clinical study aimed to evaluate and compare the effect of primary stability on osseointegration and success rate of four different implant systems. Material and Method: Eighty implants were placed on the maxillary and mandibular arch of 45 patients. The four implant systems used in this study were Straumann SLA bone level implants, BIOMET 3i OSSEOTITE, Astra Tech Dental (OsseoSpeed) Implant System, and Nobel Replace Conical Connection implant system. A two-stage implant placement procedure was followed. During the implant placement, maximum insertion torque was recorded. The implant stability quotient (ISQ) was also recorded using Ostell, which was further assessed using resonance frequency analysis (RFA). Descriptive data were analyzed using median and percentage. For Pairwise Comparison, the Shapiro-Wilks Rank Sum test was utilized. The p-value was set to 0.05 for all the measurements. Results: The insertion torque value was similar among all four implants. All the implants have almost similar ISQ values post-surgery. However, Nobel and 3i implant systems showed a lower ISQ value in the second and third quartile. Kruskal Wallis Rank Sum Test showed that the distribution of ISQ in all directions was not the same across all Implant systems (Chi-square=21.588, df=3, p-value = 0.001). The success rate of Straumann and Astra was 100%, while Nobel and 3i were 90% and 80% respectively. Conclusion: Primary stability has no effect on osseointegration and implant success rate. Moreover, Ostell device was found to be a significant predictor for implant osteointegration after successful placement and healing of dental implant site.

papers.abstract: An accuracy figure alone does not show whether the data behind it were sound or whether a single prediction deserves trust. We address both questions in a two stage framework for esophageal cancer that audits its data before reporting any result: Stage 1 recognizes Barrett’s esophagus (BE) on white light endoscopy, and Stage 2 classifies the histological subtype of a carcinoma from CT, PET and genomic data. A duplicate audit links every endoscopic image to its augmented copy before any split, and a missingness audit asks whether modality availability alone predicts the label. In Stage 1, 14 multiscale views of each image are encoded by a frozen DINOv2 backbone and scored by an ensemble of 25 members with Platt calibration, uncertainty decomposition and conformal prediction. On 204 independent test images the model reached an AUROC of 0.914 (95% CI 0.854 to 0.967), an expected calibration error of 0.044 and a calibration slope of 1.00. Epistemic uncertainty detected its errors with an AUROC of 0.898, and referring the 20% most uncertain images lowered the error rate from 7.4% to 1.8%. On the external GastroVision collection, with frozen settings, the AUROC was 0.872 (0.830 to 0.909) and uncertainty rose with dataset shift. In Stage 2, a masked attention network separated squamous cell carcinoma from adenocarcinoma with an AUROC of 0.870 (0.819 to 0.917) in 199 patients under nested cross validation. papers.title: Effects of the Flipped Classroom Model on the Learning Achievement and Communication Skills of Vocational College Students in Logistics Management
papers.abstract: Background and Aims: China's logistics market is expanding annually, and vocational education reform continues to deepen. Traditional teaching models have limitations in improving students' academic performance and communication skills. This research examines first-year logistics management students at Guangxi Vocational & Technical College of Industry to investigate the effects of flipped classrooms on their academic performance and communication skills. Methodology: This study employed a one-group pretest-posttest design. The study selected a sample of 50 first-year logistics management students from an initial population of 200 through cluster random sampling. The instructional intervention included a pre-test before, a post-test after, and eight lesson plans totaling 16 instructional hours. Communication skills were assessed using a communication ability evaluation paper, while learning achievement was measured with a learning ability evaluation paper. Data were analyzed using paired-sample t-tests and one-sample t-tests. Results: The post-test mean scores of learning achievement (M = 77.70, SD = 17.33) and communication skills (M = 38.68, SD = 3.67) were significantly higher than the pre-test scores (learning achievement: M = 48.60, SD = 8.51; communication skills: M = 22.54, SD = 4.55) at the .01 level. Both post-test means significantly exceeded the predetermined 70% criterion. Conclusion: The flipped classroom significantly improves vocational students’ learning achievement and communication skills. By promoting active learning, peer interaction, and higher-order thinking, this model supports both cognitive development and communication competence. The findings provide empirical support for applying student-centered and constructivist approaches in vocational education contexts.

papers.title: World-Model-Based Wireless Resource Allocation with Delayed Feedback
papers.abstract: Wireless resource allocation must translate delayed observations into transmission decisions. We study a hybrid world model combining an action-conditioned response predictor with a cost-aware allocator. A five-member gated recurrent unit (GRU) ensemble corrects structural transmission-error probabilities; allocation penalizes resource-block (RB) use subject to per-service predicted-utility floors. In a frozen 32-seed, 512-path evaluation under fixed control, learned estimates reduced equal-service deadline-cohort loss by 0.2525 percentage points versus the structural predictor (95% paired-bootstrap interval [−0.3272, −0.1875]). Separately, cost-plus-retention allocation reduced mean paired RB use by 28.35% versus a zero-cost policy, without establishing loss noninferiority. A prespecified comparison against a matched full-history residual multilayer perceptron on 32 additional seeds and 128 paths reduced loss by 0.0533 percentage points (95% interval [−0.0811, −0.0248]), with 0.8711% higher mean paired RB use. An autoregressive comparator and two prespecified channel/load changes likewise showed conditional loss–resource trade-offs. Service and feedback-profile effects were unequal. Adaptive planning did not outperform fixed control on reused development seeds, and computation time was excluded from packet delays. The results support a component-level allocation benefit without establishing universal architecture superiority or real-time feasibility.

papers.abstract: This study aims to describe (1) the strategies used by Islamic Religious Education and Character Education teachers to improve students’ learning motivation at SMA Negeri 2 Lambu, Bima Regency; (2) the supporting and inhibiting factors; and (3) the solutions implemented to address the inhibiting factors. This research employed a descriptive qualitative method with a phenomenological approach. The study was conducted at SMA Negeri 2 Lambu. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation involving three Islamic Religious Education teachers and five students. The data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. Data validity was examined through source, method, and time triangulation. The findings indicate that teachers applied several strategies: using digital media such as laptops and LCD projectors, conducting discussion-based learning, providing personal guidance, giving praise and additional scores, and demonstrating exemplary conduct. Supporting factors included students’ awareness of the importance of religious knowledge, their ability to read the Qur’an and hadith, and the availability of learning facilities such as a mosque, Qur’ans, and a religious library. Inhibiting factors included low learning awareness, lack of focus and active participation, late-night habits, limited study time because some students helped their parents who worked as farmers, family and peer influences, and less comfortable classroom conditions. Teachers addressed these challenges through religious habituation, motivation, personal approaches, individual guidance, and efforts to create a comfortable and active learning environment. The study highlights the importance of adapting teaching strategies to students’ needs and learning contexts.

papers.title: Влияние режимов селективного лазерного плавления на структуру и свойства биоразлагаемого сплава Fe–32Mn для медицинских имплантатов
papers.abstract: This study examined how laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), also known as selective laser melting, affects the density, microstructure, phase composition, mechanical properties, and corrosion behavior of the biodegradable Fe–32Mn alloy, a candidate material for temporary medical implants. Specimens were fabricated on a 3DLAM Mini system using a Box–Behnken design with 20 parameter sets. Laser power ranged from 160 to 280 W, scan speed from 500 to 1100 mm/s, and hatch spacing from 80 to 140 μm. The layer thickness was fixed at 40 μm, and the volumetric energy density (VED) ranged from 33 to 156 J/mm³. Density was measured by hydrostatic weighing. Microstructure was examined by scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, and phase composition was determined by X-ray diffraction. Mechanical properties were assessed by tensile testing and microhardness measurements, and corrosion behavior by potentiodynamic polarization in Hanks’ balanced salt solution at 37 °C. A VED of 60–100 J/mm³ yielded specimens with a relative density of 96–98 %. Increasing VED above 140 J/mm³ did not increase density but led to greater manganese loss. The microstructure consisted of cellular subgrains 1–3 μm in size and columnar grains aligned with the build direction. Tensile tests were performed on specimens fabricated at a VED of 113.6 J/mm³ (P = 250 W, V = 500 mm/s, h = 110 μm). Heat treatment at 1000 °C for 90 min increased the volume fraction of ε-martensite, reduced yield strength by 29.7 %, and increased elongation by 30.5%, with little change in ultimate tensile strength. The corrosion rate ranged from 0.041 to 0.053 mm/year depending on the LPBF parameters.

papers.title: THE ROLE OF AKIDAH AKHLAK TEACHER IN FOSTERING STUDENTS' RELIGIOUS CHARACTER AT MADRASAH TSANAWIYAH NEGERI 4 JAMBI CITY
papers.abstract: This study investigates the holistic role of an Akidah Akhlak teacher in shaping the religious character of students at Madrasah Tsanawiyah Negeri (MTsN) 4 Jambi City, addressing critical pedagogical gaps in adolescent moral development. Employing a qualitative descriptive case study design, this research focused on the Akidah Akhlak teacher, thirty Grade VIII C students, the madrasah head, and accompanying Islamic religious education teachers as key participants during a three-month fieldwork period from August to October 2026. Data were gathered through focused participatory observation, semi-structured in-depth interviews, and institutional documentation reviews, then analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldana, involving data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, validated through triangulation of techniques, sources, and time. The empirical findings reveal that the teacher functions dynamically as a moral role model (uswah hasanah), spiritual learning facilitator, moral motivator, and behavior evaluator. Character formation strategies encompass routine religious habituation (ta'wid), value-based active learning, and humanist-reflective discipline (ta'dhib). Furthermore, supporting factors include strong institutional leadership and religious school culture, whereas inhibiting factors stem from unmonitored digital gadget use and domestic supervision gaps. This study concludes that consistent educator role modeling and structured habituation serve as central educational practices associated with improvements in students' observable religious discipline, highlighting the need for collaborative home-school partnerships.
